text: Somanahalli Mallaiah Krishna (1 May 1932 – 10 December 2024) was an Indian politician who served as Minister of External Affairs of India from 2009 to October 2012. He was the 10th Chief Minister of Karnataka from 1999 to 2004 and the 19th Governor of Maharashtra from 2004 to 2008. He served as Speaker of the Karnataka Vidhana Soudha from December 1989 to January 1993. He was a member of both the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha from 1971 to 2014. He is widely credited with putting Bengaluru on the world map by building the foundation for it to become the IT Hub that it is today during his tenure as Chief Minister. In 2023, Krishna was awarded the Padma Vibhushan, the second highest civilian award of India. Born on 1 May 1932 to a Vokkaliga family in Somanahalli, Maddur Taluk of Mandya district, Karnataka, he completed his High School at Sri Ramakrishna Vidyashala, Mysore, and earned a Bachelor of Arts from Maharaja's College, Mysore. He obtained a law degree from University Law College, then known as Government Law College in Bangalore. He studied in the United States, graduating with a Master of Laws from Southern Methodist University in Dallas, Texas, and The George Washington University Law School in Washington D.C., where he was a Fulbright Scholar. As a student in the US, he campaigned for John F. Kennedy during the 1960 United States presidential election in areas dominated by Indian Americans; after Kennedy became President, he wrote to Krishna in 1961 expressing his "warm appreciation of your efforts during the campaign." Upon returning to India, he worked as a professor of international law at Renukacharya Law College, Bangalore. He began his electoral political career in 1962 when elected to the Mysore Legislative Assembly from Maddur as an independent, defeating K. V. Shankar Gowda, a prominent Indian National Congress (INC) leader for whom Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru had campaigned. He joined the Praja Socialist Party (PSP) but lost to M. Manchegowda of the INC in the 1967 election. He was elected to the Lok Sabha in 1968 at by-polls from Mandya following the death of the sitting parliamentarian. In 1968, he played a key role in reconciling members of the Indian National Congress and the PSP. He served three terms as a member of parliament from Mandya, starting with the 1968 by-poll as a PSP candidate, followed by wins in 1971 and 1980. He resigned from the Lok Sabha in 1972, joined the Karnataka Legislative Council, and was appointed a minister by Devaraj Urs. After returning to the Lok Sabha in 1980, he served as a minister under Indira Gandhi between 1983 and 1984. He lost his bid for the Mandya Lok Sabha seat in the 1984 elections but was reelected to the Karnataka Legislative Assembly in 1985. He served as Speaker of the Karnataka Legislative Assembly from 18 December 1989 to 20 January 1993 and as Deputy Chief Minister of Karnataka from 1993 to 1994. He was a member of the Rajya Sabha from April 1996 to 1999. In 1999, as president of the Karnataka Pradesh Congress Committee, he led his party to victory in the assembly polls and became Chief Minister of Karnataka, a position he held until being defeated in the 2004 Karnataka Legislative Assembly elections. He was instrumental in creating power reforms with ESCOMS and digitizing land records through the BHOOMI initiative, and promoted private-public participation, sponsoring the Bangalore Advance Task Force. He was appointed Governor of Maharashtra on 6 December 2004 and resigned on 5 March 2008, reportedly to return to active politics in Karnataka; President Pratibha Patil accepted his resignation on 6 March. He entered the Rajya Sabha and took oath as Union Cabinet Minister of External Affairs under Prime Minister Manmohan Singh on 22 May 2009. During his tenure, he visited countries including Tajikistan in 2012 to strengthen economic and energy ties. He resigned as External Affairs Minister on 26 October 2012, signaling a return to Karnataka state politics. On 29 January 2017, he resigned from the Indian National Congress, citing the party's "state of confusion" regarding its need for mass leaders and claiming he had been sidelined, stating the party was "dependent on managers and not time-tested people like himself." After speculation about joining the Bharatiya Janata Party, he formally joined the party in March 2017. He announced his retirement from politics in January 2023, citing age-related issues. He was married to Prema and had two daughters; his daughter Malavika Krishna was married to the Late V. G. Siddhartha, a businessman and founder of Cafe Coffee Day. He had a younger brother, Shankar (who died in 2019), who was a member of the Karnataka Legislative Council. At the end of his political life, he released his biography, Smritivahini, in the presence of many dignitaries, including anecdotes such as the Veerappan kidnapping of Rajkumar during his tenure as Chief Minister, and noted that former Prime Minister H. D. Devegowda had strong plans to join the Indian National Congress twice during the period of National Emergency. He died from a long illness at his residence in Bengaluru on 10 December 2024, at the age of 92. He was cremated with state honours, including a gun salute, at his ancestral village of Somanahalli in Maddur taluk of Mandya district on 11 December. The Karnataka Government declared a three-day mourning period.
